flags.ask: Confirm the bolt size for the leg-to-beam bolt (8-15/16" of wood), the 2-9/16" of leg left at the bolt after the flush cut, and how the head and nut bear on the leg's tilted outer face.
flags.why: This joint and the gusset carry the beam and every swing load.

flags.ask: Confirm the frame on sloped ground: leg lengths, footing or burial on the downhill side, and whether to regrade instead.
flags.why: The CPSC home handbook recommends a level site to reduce the chance of tipping (Pub. 324, p. 2).

flags.ask: Confirm the burial depth (24"), that the leg lumber is rated for ground contact, and whether it needs UC4B (heavy duty) rather than UC4A.
flags.why: Buried legs anchor the frame against lifting and walking, and wood decays fastest at the ground line. AWPA U1 puts parts in ground contact that are critical or hard to replace under UC4B.

flags.ask: Crossbar to leg, 2 × 1/2" bolts: leg edge distance 1-3/4" (3.5D): under 4D (2") for minimum, the edge the load pushes toward. Confirm the bolt size and layout with these distances.
flags.why: NDS 2024 12.5.1 sets these distances for bolts in wood (Tables 12.5.1A to 12.5.1D). Below a full-value distance, the joint is designed for less load.

flags.ask: Gusset to leg, 2 × 1/2" bolts: leg edge distance 1-3/4" (3.5D): under 4D (2") for minimum, the edge the load pushes toward. gusset edge distance under the beam's weight, to the top edge 1-13/16" (3.6D): under 4D (2") for minimum, the edge the load pushes toward. Confirm the bolt size and layout with these distances.
flags.why: NDS 2024 12.5.1 sets these distances for bolts in wood (Tables 12.5.1A to 12.5.1D). Below a full-value distance, the joint is designed for less load.

flags.ask: For the bolts' end distance, the crossbar ends 1-5/8", 2' 10-1/2" to 3' 4" above the ground, and the gusset ends 1-5/8", 7' 4-3/4" to 8' 0" above the ground project past the legs. Confirm the projecting ends are acceptable where children play, with their edges and corners eased.
flags.why: The projecting ends are new to this design, and children reach the crossbar.

flags.ask: Choose the order the frame goes up in. The steps stand each A-frame up and brace it, then lift the beam onto the gussets and drill and bolt it between the leg tops there. The other order lays the A-frames on their sides, bolts the beam between them on the ground, and tips the whole frame up into place.
flags.why: The first lifts the beam 96" up onto frames held only by temporary braces, and drills through the leg tops from a ladder. The second does all the drilling and bolting on the ground, but lifts the whole frame at once, a heavier and more awkward load that needs more helpers. OSHA asks for two or more people on any load over 50 pounds (Electrical Contractors eTool, Heavy Lifting).

assumptions: Supported at the middle of each gusset's top edge under the beam, 11-1/4" and 108-3/4" from the left end. The beam rests on the gussets, and the leg-to-beam bolts sit in holes 1/16" larger than the bolt, so the gussets take the beam's weight and the swing loads first.

NDS 2024 3.2.1 takes the span from face to face of the supports plus half the bearing length needed at each end. That bearing can be no longer than the gusset's, so the span to the middle of each gusset is the longest it allows and gives the largest bending moment.

Each hanger's bolt goes down through the beam on its centerline, in a 9/16" hole (the bolt plus 1/16", NDS 2024 12.1.3.2). Its washer bears on the beam's top, so bending and shear are taken on the net section there.
Deflection uses the beam's gross section; the holes are not deducted from its stiffness.
Each A-frame holds the beam against rotation at its support (legs bolted against both faces, gusset underneath), so the unbraced length is the span.
The beam's own weight acts as a uniform load over the span, from its density at the entered moisture content; seats and chains are in the rider weights.
Simply supported between the two supports; loads outside the supports, including the weight of any overhang, are not part of this check.
Smooth pendulum: chain tension at the bottom of the arc is W·(3 − 2·cos θ) for a rider of weight W swinging to θ from vertical.
Both swings are at the bottom of their arcs at the same time (riders in sync), so their loads add.
Each swing's load is split equally between its two hangers (a centered rider).
The dynamic factor covers snap loads from slack chains, which exceed the smooth pendulum load. It is not applied to the beam's own weight.
formulas: Each point load P = C_dyn · its load before the factor; the uniform load w is not multiplied
R1 = Σ P·(L − a) / L + w·L / 2, R2 = Σ P·a / L + w·L / 2 (a = distance of each load from the left support)
M(x) = R1·x − w·x² / 2 − Σ P·(x − a) over loads left of x; the largest M is where the shear changes sign
S = b·d² / 6
f_b = M / S
At each hole, S_net is the section modulus of the gross section less the hole, and f_b = M(x) / S_net there
f_b = the largest of these
Fb' = Fb · C_D · C_M · C_t · C_L · C_F · C_fu · C_i · C_r
margin = Fb' / f_b

NDS 2024 3.2.1 takes the span from face to face of the supports plus half the bearing length needed at each end. That bearing can be no longer than the gusset's, so the span to the middle of each gusset is the longest it allows and gives the largest bending moment.

flags.ask: Choose the order the frame goes up in. The steps stand each A-frame up and brace it, then lift the beam onto the gussets and drill and bolt it between the leg tops there. flags.ask: Choose the order the frame goes up in. The steps stand each A-frame up and brace it, then lift the beam onto the gussets and drill and bolt it between the leg tops there. The other order lays the A-frames on their sides, bolts the beam between them on the ground, and tips the whole frame up into place.

The second does all the drilling and bolting on the ground, but lifts the whole frame at once, a heavier and more awkward load that needs more helpers. Supported at the middle of each gusset's top edge under the beam, 11-1/4" and 108-3/4" from the left end. The beam rests on the gussets, and the leg-to-beam bolts sit in holes 1/16" larger than the bolt, so the gussets take the beam's weight and the swing loads first.

NDS 2024 3.2.1 takes the span from face to face of the supports plus half the bearing length needed at each end. That bearing can be no longer than the gusset's, so the span to the middle of each gusset is the longest it allows and gives the largest bending moment.

Each hanger's bolts cross the beam in one row, 1-1/2" above its bottom, in 7/16" holes (the bolt plus 1/16", NDS 2024 12.1.3.2). Bending is taken at the hanger's position with one hole in the section; bolts one above another are not covered. The seat hangs from the bolts, so shear there is taken on the beam's depth below them (NDS 2024 3.4.4.1).
Deflection uses the beam's gross section; the holes are not deducted from its stiffness.
Each A-frame holds the beam against rotation at its support (legs bolted against both faces, gusset underneath), so the unbraced length is the span.
The beam's own weight acts as a uniform load over the span, from its density at the entered moisture content; seats and chains are in the rider weights.

Smooth pendulum: chain tension at the bottom of the arc is W·(3 − 2·cos θ) for a rider of weight W swinging to θ from vertical.
Both swings are at the bottom of their arcs at the same time (riders in sync), so their loads add.
Each swing's load is split equally between its two hangers (a centered rider).
The dynamic factor covers snap loads from slack chains, which exceed the smooth pendulum load. It is not applied to the beam's own weight.

checklist.element: Leg-to-beam bolt and gusset, each frame
checklist.confirm: Bolt size (1/2", 8-7/16" grip), edge and end distances in the legs and beam, washers on the tilted outer faces, and that the gusset and bolt together carry the beam's reaction.
checklist.why: Each frame carries half of every swing load into the legs through this joint; connections are not computed.

checklist.confirm: Ply bolt pattern and spacing (6 bolts entered), and that every hanger's load reaches all 2 plies.
checklist.why: The checks assume each ply carries an equal share of every load (decision 0013); that holds only if the plies are fastened together and every load reaches every ply.

checklist.confirm: That each frame holds the beam against rolling over at its support.
checklist.why: The beam stability factor assumes it; without that restraint the beam can buckle sideways at a lower load.

checklist.confirm: That the frames resist side-to-side and front-to-back swing forces without racking, and whether corner braces are needed.
checklist.why: Swinging pushes the top of the frame back and forth. Along the beam, on pads, nothing in the frames themselves holds them: each foot can turn on its pad and each frame about its leg-to-beam bolt, so only how tightly the bolts clamp, the ground anchors, or corner braces keep the frames from leaning. Racking is not computed.

checklist.confirm: Anchor type and count (1 per foot), that the rated pull-out holds in this soil, how each anchor is fastened to its leg, and how they are buried or covered.
checklist.why: The anchor check gives the pull on one anchor from the swing alone; the soil, the fastening to the leg, and sliding along the ground are not computed.

checklist.confirm: Hangers rated for swing use, installed through the beam as the manufacturer specifies, with holes no larger and no lower in the beam than the bending and shear checks take.
checklist.why: The hanger margin uses the manufacturer's rating, which holds only for its specified installation.

checklist.confirm: Boards free of large knots near the edges (especially near midspan of the beam), steep grain slope, splits, and wane.
checklist.why: Design values assume the grade; a defect in the wrong place lowers strength more than the grade allows for.

checklist.confirm: An inspection routine: nuts and bolts twice a month, seats and chains monthly (CPSC Pub. 324, p. 5), and decay at the ground line.
checklist.why: Wood shrinks and bolts loosen, especially in pressure-treated lumber that was sold wet.
